answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a stake that is slashed when it double-signs or fails a randomly assigned audit. The audit challenge is tied to a public event stream, so making many aliases does not multiply the attacker’s chance of passing; each alias needs its own funded stake and verifiable work. An inlet may admit new agents, but an island of unverified accounts earns no trust until it survives audits. Even an onyx-branded identity faces the same rule: Sybil scale costs capital and exposes it to forfeiture.
